candidates.lead: One man says he is "like a zombie" due to not being able to sleep through lorries driving past his house
candidates.evidence_text: 'M67 motorway closures mean I can't sleep at night' - BBC News Image caption, Francoise Sullivan said additional traffic noise caused by lorries being diverted from the M67 was keeping her and her husband awake at night By Richard Stead North West Published 1 hour ago A couple have said they cannot sleep due to traffic being diverted past their home at night during long-running motorway improvements. The M67 has been closed in both directions on weeknights between 20:00 and 06:00 since July and lorries and cars will continue to be diverted onto Mottram Road, in Godley, Tameside, until December. Francoise Sullivan, who has lived on the road since 1987, said: "It's a nightmare - we just can't sleep from the noise and the vibrations. We've been given some medication but it doesn't really help because the house shakes, the bed shakes and we worry what it's doing to our house." National Highways said it "understands" the impact roadworks can have on local people. Image caption, Work is taking place at the M67 Junction 4 roundabout as part of the Mottram bypass scheme Image caption, John Sullivan said HGVs should be directed away from Mottram Road when the M67 is closed John Sullivan said: "You can't relax in your own home and you can't sleep at night because you're waiting for the next lorry." The 75-year-old former Tameside mayor added: "I'm like a zombie in the daytime and it's an absolutely dreadful, dreadful way to have to live." On one night when the M67 was closed, the couple say they counted 758 HGVs and 4,609 cars passing their home in Godley between 20:00 and 06:00. The couple have also urged Tameside Council to resurface Mottram Road and impose a reduced speed limit to minimise noise. The regular closure of the M67 is part of the A57 Link Roads scheme, designed to take traffic travelling between Manchester and Sheffield away from the village of Mottram in Longdendale. Construction of the bypass is set to be completed during the winter of 2028-29. Image source, John Sullivan Image caption, Traffic is being diverted onto Mottram Road during the M67 overnight closures Karen Cliffe, National Highways' programme manager, said: "We understand the impact roadworks can have and we've met with Mr and Mrs Sullivan to explain our approach. "We carefully planned this work to minimise disruption and, in partnership with Tameside Council, determined that the A57 is an appropriate diversion route because it accepts all forms of motorway traffic, including HGVs." A council spokesperson said: "We appreciate the disturbance that increased traffic levels, particularly HGV movements, may be causing to residents along the diversion route. "Classified routes like Mottram Road are designed to convey the majority of traffic through the borough and we are obliged to agree to the diversion but we're liaising with National Highways to look at how they can mitigate the impact on local residents." Image caption, Reform UK councillor Allan Hopwood said the overnight closures were causing too much disruption The work on the A57 Link Roads scheme has meant the remodelling of the roundabout at the end of the M67 in Mottram. Farmer Allan Hopwood, who lives nearby and is the leader of Reform UK on Tameside Council, said: "It's been an absolute disaster from start to finish because it's meant extra traffic through Hattersley and through the centre of Mottram. "If I want to cross the roundabout, I have to make a phone call to get a chaperone who can escort me across the site but I've sometimes had to wait 45 minutes for somebody to let me in to my own land." candidates.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

candidates.lead: The Golden Garter opened its doors in the Wythenshawe area of Manchester in 1968 and attracted huge stars
candidates.evidence_text: Wythenshawe 100: Cabaret club on Europe's biggest council estate - BBC News Image source, John Orchard Image caption, The Golden Garter in Wythenshawe proved to be a popular venue when it opened in 1968 By Kaya Black and Lauren Hirst , North West Published 19 October 2026 When the Golden Garter cabaret club opened its doors for the first time in October 1968, TV legend Sir Bruce Forsyth was the first name on the door. Situated on a council estate in the Wythenshawe area of Manchester, people travelled from far and wide to enjoy shows at the 1,400-capacity venue. From music stars Dusty Springfield, Roy Orbison and Eartha Kitt to comedians Tommy Cooper and Ronnie Corbett, there was never a shortage of acts wanting to appear. "I think Dusty Springfield was the big highlight for me," said 79-year-old John Orchard, who was a pianist for Shep's Banjo Boys from 1969 to 1972. "She was my favourite singer in the 1960s and all of a sudden there she is at the Golden Garter. "This is a nightclub in Wythenshawe under the flight path of the Ringway airport (now known as Manchester Airport) in the middle of the biggest council estate in Europe. "So it was a bit incongruous, but it was a fantastic place and Wythenshawe loved it and it loved Wythenshawe." Image source, Unknown Image caption, The Golden Garter could pack in crowds of up to 1,400 The Golden Garter holds many happy memories for Paul Stoloff, who was a bassist for the Golden Garter Showband from 1970 to 1982. "It was good fun - happy times," he said. "It was interesting because it was different music every week. "So if you didn't like what they're doing, it'd be different for the next week." With so many famous faces descending on the club over its 14-year life, there are plenty of tales from behind the scenes. "I remember one night when Dusty Springfield was on, I can even remember the blue dress that she was wearing," said Margaret Giannini, who worked at the club from 1967 to 1980. "Anyway, something happened that she wasn't too happy about and she walked off the stage and went backstage and wouldn't come out. "The lighting man at the time came backstage and said to her 'Oi - you get back on that stage and earn your money' and what did she do? She went straight back on the stage." The Golden Garter proved so popular that even Queen Elizabeth II's sister Princess Margaret paid a visit to the venue on Rowlands Way for a Royal Charity Gala. Image source, Margaret Giannini Image caption, The venue's staff were always excited to meet the stars who graced the stage Customers could treat themselves to a three-course meal for just 15 shillings (75p) while watching what was described as "uninterrupted views" of the stage. From smoked Scottish salmon with brown bread and butter to a peach melba, a range of dishes was designed to suit all taste buds. "Oh, it was unbelievable - it was a good night out," said Peter Andrews. "People used to dress up in the finery and used to get chicken in the basket and stuff like that for something to eat." The Golden Garter shut its doors on New Year's Eve in 1982, with The Fortunes bringing down the curtain. "It's a different time now - there's nothing to indicate what it was and no-one would believe it because this is Wythenshawe," said Margaret. Those who were there, though, definitely remember. BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people about their lives in Wythenshawe to mark 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation. You can read more here . candidates.evidence_text: Murder investigation launched after woman's death - BBC News Image caption, Greater Manchester Police is appealing for information By Naj Modak North West Published 19 October 2026 A murder investigation has been launched after a woman was found dead at a property in Manchester. Officers were called to reports of a disturbance at an address on Crondall Street in Moss Side at about 13:30 BST. Emergency services found the body of a woman and a 26-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of murder. Det Ch Insp Louise Edwards said police believed the incident was isolated and there was no wider threat to the community. A scene remains in place while officers carry out enquiries. Edwards added: "We would ask that people stay away from the scene and we'd like to thank the local community for their patience while officers undertake their work." Greater Manchester Police is asking anyone with information to get in touch. candidates.lead: Smith, from Liverpool, is alleged to have inflicted serious facial injuries on a concierge worker
candidates.evidence_text: Former world champion boxer Liam Smith is alleged to have punched a man in the head as he lay on the floor "unable to stand", a court heard Smith, who held the WBO light-middleweight title from 2015 to 2016, appeared for the first time at Manchester Crown Court earlier to face a charge of causing grievous bodily harm with intent The 38-year-old, from Liverpool, was not asked to enter pleas to the charge which followed his arrest for the alleged attack on a concierge worker at The Blade tower block on Silvercroft Street, Deansgate, on 13 September Alleged victim Laurent Nke suffered facial injuries and spent time in hospital, the court heard During a brief hearing Judge Tom Gilbart referred to the fact the incident was captured on CCTV cameras He said: "Part of the footage shows the defendant deliver two strikes to the head of somebody lying on the floor who's unable to stand."

candidates.evidence_text: Drivers face one-hour delays after crash closes M6 - BBC News Image source, Highways England Image caption, A crash between a van and a lorry caused the M6 to be closed Published 19 October 2026 Drivers are facing delays of up to an hour after a crash between a van and a lorry closed a section of the M6 in both directions. The motorway has been shut been junction 23 in Newton-le-Willows, Merseyside, and junction 24 in Ashton-in-Makerfield, Greater Manchester, National Highways said. Merseyside Police said the crash at 22:00 BST on Sunday resulted in a vehicle fire with Merseyside Fire and Rescue also at the scene alongside its officers. The southbound carriageway was opened at 07:30 but the northbound carriageway remains closed. Diversions have been put in place. National Highways said: "Specialist clear up works to remove burnt out debris is ongoing." candidates.lead: David Chipfupa could not find any network for black professionals in Manchester so started his own
candidates.evidence_text: After struggling to find a network for black entrepreneurs, a Manchester-based businessman said he decided to start his own David Chipfupa moved from Berkshire four years ago for a change of lifestyle But the 37-year-old said working remotely in technology sales soon left him feeling professionally isolated "I didn't really see a space where black professionals could network," he said. "There were events but there wasn't really a community in Manchester. Now our community is a celebration of black success and black excellence every day." Since Chipfupa founded Afrosocial in 2024 the network now has more than 4,000 members and has reached Australia, Dubai, South Africa and the United States "I wasn't going to the office and it was isolating," David told the BBC

candidates.evidence_text: Film director Danny Boyle said his new film about the rise of The Sun newspaper does not shy away from its coverage of the Hillsborough disaster The Oscar-winning director from Bury said the 1989 headline 'The Truth', which falsely blamed Liverpool fans for the tragedy, was "one of the darkest days in publishing history" Boyle made the comments at a screening of Ink in Manchester ahead of the film's release next year The film, due to stream on Netflix next year, stars Guy Pearce as media mogul Rupert Murdoch, Jack O'Connell as editor Larry Lamb and Claire Foy as a reporter Despite what he described as the "disgrace of Hillsborough", Boyle said he took on the project because he saw parallels between the newspaper's rise and today's "clickbait world", adding that Fleet Street during that era was a "riveting piece of British history" Speaking to BBC North West Tonight , Boyle said the film "doesn't shy away" from The Sun's coverage of the Hillsborough disaster

candidates.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

candidates.evidence_text: A new railway station is to be built in Bradford which will put the city at the "heart" of the Northern Powerhouse Railway network, the government has confirmed The station, which will replace Bradford Interchange, will be delivered in the 2030s and provide improved links to Leeds, York and Manchester, a spokesperson said The Northern Powerhouse Rail (NPR) scheme was first proposed over a decade ago, but in January the government promised the £45bn plan would go ahead Mayor of West Yorkshire Tracy Brabin said the government's latest confirmation the station would be built in the city was an "iron-clad commitment" "Today is an exciting and important milestone for Bradford," Brabin said "Bradford has so much untapped potential, and faster, more frequent trains to Leeds and Manchester, and the transformation of the city centre through Bradford City Village, will help to finally unleash it."

candidates.evidence_text: Education Greater Manchester's three worst schools for truancy named - see where yours ranks with our interactive map Unauthorised absence rates are still around twice as high as pre-pandemic levels Add to preferred sources Comments News Annie Gouk an School attendance rates have never returned to pre-pandemic levels and despite improving over the last couple of years, the rate of unauthorised absences is still around twice as high as before Covid It's an issue facing most schools and parents are sent regular reminders over the impact that lost learning has on attainment Despite some improvement, the figures remain bleak and across all state funded secondary schools in England, unauthorised absences made up around 2.9% of all school sessions in the autumn and spring term 2025/26 - equating to nearly 12 million school days missed While around 1.1 million were lost to both term-time holidays and lateness, the vast majority - 9.3 million - were due to 'other' reasons These can include things like missing school for family birthdays, shopping trips, car trouble, or youngsters truanting without their parents’ knowledge or permission

But customer numbers are falling, with those in charge pointing the fingers at ‘degraded’ and outdated buildings Garden centres are no longer just a shopping destination, but are expected to be a more rounded experience with dining and refreshments now key parts of the offer, planning documents state. While ‘quaint’, the café at Newbank is ‘terribly degraded’ and ‘too small’, they add Newbank Garden Centre continued: “As much as we try to paper over the cracks with our displays and exciting products, the infrastructure of the site is now starting to let us down quite badly.” The centre has now received permission from Bury council to implement a plan it considers to be ‘essential to the longevity of the business’. This will see a ‘much improved and larger’ café created, along with modernised toilets

candidates.evidence_text: Education Greater Manchester's three worst schools for truancy named - see where yours ranks with our interactive map Unauthorised absence rates are still around twice as high as pre-pandemic levels Add to preferred sources Comments News Annie Gouk an School attendance rates have never returned to pre-pandemic levels and despite improving over the last couple of years, the rate of unauthorised absences is still around twice as high as before Covid It's an issue facing most schools and parents are sent regular reminders over the impact that lost learning has on attainment Despite some improvement, the figures remain bleak and across all state funded secondary schools in England, unauthorised absences made up around 2.9% of all school sessions in the autumn and spring term 2025/26 - equating to nearly 12 million school days missed While around 1.1 million were lost to both term-time holidays and lateness, the vast majority - 9.3 million - were due to 'other' reasons These can include things like missing school for family birthdays, shopping trips, car trouble, or youngsters truanting without their parents’ knowledge or permission

В результате атаки погиб второй человек, Адриан Долби, который был случайно ранен полицейским, когда помогал забаррикадировать двери синагоги. Passengers have been warned the disruption is expected to last until at least 12pm National Rail said: "A failure of the electricity supply in the Preston area means some lines are disrupted. As a result, trains between Preston and Bolton may be cancelled, revised, delayed by up to 45 minutes or diverted. Disruption is expected until 12:00." Northern said all lines are blocked between Preston and Bolton, with the route between Millom/Barrow-in-Furness/Windermere/Blackpool North and Manchester Airport affected. candidates.evidence_text: Radcliffe The Greater Manchester garden centre being 'badly let down' is set for change Those in charge have set out a plan to secure the centres future Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:25, 20 Oct 2026 Updated 06:29, 20 Oct A Greater Manchester garden centre said it must evolve to secure its future Newbank Garden Centre, in Radcliffe , says it is one of the ‘most recognisable businesses in the area’ and ‘one of the leading independent garden centres in England’. But customer numbers are falling, with those in charge pointing the fingers at ‘degraded’ and outdated buildings Garden centres are no longer just a shopping destination, but are expected to be a more rounded experience with dining and refreshments now key parts of the offer, planning documents state. While ‘quaint’, the café at Newbank is ‘terribly degraded’ and ‘too small’, they add Newbank Garden Centre continued: “As much as we try to paper over the cracks with our displays and exciting products, the infrastructure of the site is now starting to let us down quite badly.” The centre has now received permission from Bury council to implement a plan it considers to be ‘essential to the longevity of the business’. This will see a ‘much improved and larger’ café created, along with modernised toilets

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport 'When the doctor told me I had lung cancer I was gobsmacked. I'd had no symptoms' "I actually had to ask them if they were sure they had the right person because I felt fine!” Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 06:08 A former pub landlady found out she had cancer after an impromptu pit stop during one of her dog walks Jean Page, 73, was on a leisurely stroll with her dog when she decided to get herself checked out a mobile clinic which had parked up on Hazel Grove Park and Ride in Stockport The clinic on wheels was an NHS lung health check facility which smokers and former smokers aged between 55 and 75 are encouraged to visit when they see them dotted around Greater Manchester A smoker of 50 years, Jean didn't have any symptoms, but knew friends who had undergone the screen and she decided to follow suit When inside, the grandma-of-six filled out a questionnaire and underwent a CT scan. A few days later she received a follow up call inviting her for further tests at the hospital

candidates.evidence_text: Education Greater Manchester's three worst schools for truancy named - see where yours ranks with our interactive map Unauthorised absence rates are still around twice as high as pre-pandemic levels Add to preferred sources Comments News Annie Gouk an School attendance rates have never returned to pre-pandemic levels and despite improving over the last couple of years, the rate of unauthorised absences is still around twice as high as before Covid It's an issue facing most schools and parents are sent regular reminders over the impact that lost learning has on attainment Despite some improvement, the figures remain bleak and across all state funded secondary schools in England, unauthorised absences made up around 2.9% of all school sessions in the autumn and spring term 2025/26 - equating to nearly 12 million school days missed While around 1.1 million were lost to both term-time holidays and lateness, the vast majority - 9.3 million - were due to 'other' reasons These can include things like missing school for family birthdays, shopping trips, car trouble, or youngsters truanting without their parents’ knowledge or permission

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Knifeman tried to murder stranger and attacked three others in Altrincham, jury told Nathan Peters denies attempted murder Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 18:12, 19 Oct 2026 View Image Police at the scene in Altrinc A knifeman tried to murder a stranger during a series of random attacks on revellers in Altrincham town centre, a trial has heard Nathan Peters is accused of attempted murder after stabbing Max Morrison in the early hours. He denies the charge Peters has admitted assaulting three other people, including ‘slashing’ the face of Mr Morrison’s friend Harrison Brannan. He punched a man named Marvin-Jay Speakman and pushed over his partner Melissa Mellor to the floor in the town centre Peters is standing trial at Minshull Street Crown Court. Prosecuting, Jonathan Dickinson said: “The defendant, apparently himself on a night out, carried out a series of unprovoked attacks on people who had no connection with him and just happened to be in the wrong place at the Jurors were told there is a ‘narrow issue’ in the case, to decide whether Peters intended to kill Mr Morrison. Mr Dickinson added: “There are no real factual disputes between the prosecution and the defence.”

It would see a total of 403 homes built, with a mix of houses, bungalows and flats proposed Developer Wain Homes said the land, off Castle Road, forms part of the Northern Gateway development area which has been allocated for housing and industrial development through the Places for Everyone plan. That allocation has seen swathes of countryside removed from the green be Included in the wider masterplan are up to 1,550 new homes, a new primary school and ‘community facilities’ at Simister and Bowlee. Meanwhile, land at Heywood and Pilsworth, between junctions 18 and 19 of the M62 , would see a 6.5 million square foot industrial estate with shops, The 403-home plan has two parts to it. Full planning permission is being sought from Bury council for 283 of the properties which will occupy around three-quarters of the site

candidates.evidence_text: M56 "His beautiful daughter will never know the real Cody": Family pay tribute to man killed in M56 police chase "Cody was turning his life around. The knowledge that his beautiful daughter will never know the real Cody that we all knew and loved is a The family of a man who died following a crash on the M56 this weekend have paid tribute. In a statement issued through Greater Manchester Police, the family of Cody Lowndes said he was in the process of turning his life around The 27-year-old died after being struck by a vehicle on the motorway on Saturday evening (October 17). Before the crash, he was spotted driving a motorbike 'in a dangerous manner' on the M60 near Stockport Pyramid Police began a pursuit which continued onto the M56. Greater Manchester Police said 'tactical contact' was then made with the biker near junction five at Hale Barns The chase continued and the motorbike was 'brought to a stop' near Wythenshawe , the force said. GMP said that the driver of the motorbike then 'made off on foot across the motorway' He was then involved in a collision with another vehicle. He sadly died on the scene

candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 14 October 2026 at 10:33am Kirith Entwistle, the Labour MP for Bolton North East, has said she found the current court system "triggering" and had to watch her abuser "stare at her". Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

Credit: 499883 A man who murdered a mother and four of her children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police despite Zak Bolland, 26, walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute ‘no comment’ interview for breaking the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Jackson Street in Walkden, Greater Manchester on November 26 2017 Bolland’s previous convictions and suspended jail sentence he was serving at the time had not been checked by police and he was told he would be ‘NFA’d’ – no further action taken against him over the windows attack, Bolton Coroner’s Court heard Thirteen days later, in the dead of night on December 11 2017, he smashed Ms Pearson’s windows again and tossed in a petrol bomb which “exploded” near the stairs, blocking the only exit to the ground floor and trapping the victims upstairs Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, all died in the blaze Ms Pearson suffered 68% burns to her body and “clung on to life” until she died, 20 months after the attack on August 25 2019

candidates.title: Intercompany transactions: five examples explained | About Manchester
candidates.summary: A £900 sale between two subsidiaries is revenue for the seller, yet contributes no external revenue to the group. The difference lies in whose accounts you are reading. Intercompany transactions are exchanges between separate companies within a corporate group, including a parent
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Validator: corrected section routing before translation (section_routing:it_content). | Selection: Board rejected: too_thin, outside_scope

candidates.lead: A £900 sale between two subsidiaries is revenue for the seller, yet contributes no external revenue to the group.
candidates.evidence_text: A £900 sale between two subsidiaries is revenue for the seller, yet contributes no external revenue to the group. The difference lies in whose accounts you are reading Intercompany transactions are exchanges between separate companies within a corporate group, including a parent and subsidiary or two subsidiaries. Each records its own side of the transaction; consolidated accounts present the included companies as one economic entity. A charge These illustrative examples assume wholly owned companies included in the same consolidation and set aside tax, currency and impairment effects Company A buys stock from an external supplier for £600, then sells it to Company B for £900. A records £900 revenue and £600 cost of sales; B records £900 inventory At group level, the internal sale is eliminated from revenue. Finance teams can use financial consolidation software to support that process, working from records that identify the other company and transaction amount Suppose all the stock remains unsold to external customers at the reporting date. B’s £900 inventory includes £300 profit made inside the group. Eliminating this unrealised profit reduces group inventory to its original £600 cost and removes the internal gain from group profit

candidates.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

The internal document – that will be shared with council workers tomorrow and is based on a survey of nearly 1,200 staff – The report describes a culture at the council in which senior staff can act inappropriately with seeming impunity. Many junior staff members believe raising issues will lead to retaliation, and 59% of survey respondents have witnessed or experienced a form of harassment, discrimi One worker recalled a young apprentice being repeatedly sexually harassed by a senior colleague until she was forced to leave the council. “He was allowed to stay,” they said of the offending staffer. “She was interviewed by two male managers and needless to say she left.” There A council worker, speaking to us on the condition of anonymity, said of the report: “if I were a manager that would sicken me to my core.” When we approached the council before publishing this story, CEO Tom Stannard said: “it is completely unacceptable that anyone should feel undervalued, unable to raise concerns, unsupported if they do or – in the worst cases – unsafe. These issues cannot and will not be ignored.”

candidates.title: Local residents could get £500 towards electric car charging system under new plans
candidates.summary: The scheme would be delivered in partnership with Kerbo Charge
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Selected in last_24h shortlist before writing.
candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: The scheme would be delivered in partnership with Kerbo Charge
candidates.evidence_text: Local residents could get £500 towards electric car charging system under new plans Skip to content News — Transport Local residents could get £500 towards electric car charging system under new plans The scheme would be delivered in partnership with Kerbo Charge. , and David Prior October 19, 2026 . 9:55 AM 2 min read Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pinterest Share on LinkedIn Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Residents in Altrincham and across Trafford who don't have a driveway could soon be able to charge their electric cars at home using special channels installed in the pavement. Trafford Council's Executive will consider proposals tonight for a one-year trial that would allow homeowners to install recessed charging cable channels across public footpaths, with the first 240 successful applicants receiving a £500 discount. The scheme would be delivered in partnership with Kerbo Charge, whose system allows an electric vehicle charging cable to run through a narrow channel between a property and a parked car. A flexible, self-closing lid sits flush with the pavement when the cable is removed, avoiding the trip hazards associated with cables trailing across footpaths. The proposals could particularly benefit residents living in terraced properties and other homes without driveways. According to a report prepared for Trafford Council's Executive, approximately 28% of households in the borough do not have off-street parking. The council currently prohibits residents from running charging cables across public footpaths, even when covered by protective mats, because of safety and accessibility concerns. However, officers say they have received increasing numbers of enquiries from residents seeking alternative charging solutions. Under the proposed scheme, installations would normally cost £1,731.15 upfront, but a £500 government-funded discount would reduce this to £1,231.15 for the first 240 approved applicants. A maintenance subscription of approximately £4.15 per month would also apply after the first two years. Not every property would qualify - applications would be assessed individually, taking into account pavement width, parking restrictions, road safety and the potential impact on pedestrians. Residents would also need appropriate public liability insurance, while an approved installation would not guarantee a parking space outside their home. The council has secured £132,735 from the government's Office for Zero Emission Vehicles to support the initiative. If approved tonight, the trial could begin during the third quarter of the 2026/27 financial year, subject to anticipated changes to national planning rules. The government is expected to remove the requirement for planning permission to install electric vehicle chargers at homes without off-street parking, although the change has yet to come into force. Once approved, installations would be carried out by Kerbo Charge, with a target completion time of approximately six weeks following payment. candidates.evidence_text: The report also proposes charges at Thorley Lane car park in Timperley, which is currently free Share on WhatsApp Share via Email The report proposes charges at Thorley Lane car park in Timperley, which is currently free Motorists in Altrincham could face parking charges until 8pm and on Sundays under new proposals put forward by Trafford Council The changes form part of the council's draft budget for 2027/28, which aims to raise an additional £250,000 a year from parking charges across the borough The proposals include extending on-street charging hours in Altrincham, Sale and parts of Stretford, alongside revised tariffs for council-owned car parks, the introduction of Sunday charging and extended charging hours from 8am to 8pm In Altrincham, council-operated car parks include Regent Road and Oakfield Road, while nearby council car parks include Cecil Road, Victoria Road and Brown Street in Hale, and Balmoral Road and Baker Street in Timperley Currently, charges at these car parks generally apply between 8am and 6pm, Monday to Saturday, with parking free on Sundays

candidates.evidence_text: A report going to the Council’s Executive committee this week (Weds 14 October) charts record numbers of affordable homes being delivered in wards across Manchester to meet city-wide demand Data broken down by Council ward shows how affordable housing investment in communities – particularly in north and east Manchester and Wythenshawe – is helping to meet an ambitious target to help deliver at least 10,000 social rent, Council and genuinely affordable homes up to 2 Now nearly halfway through the Housing Strategy period from 2022, when combining affordable completions with developments on site and alongside housing in the future pipeline, the city is already close to securing development to meet the 10,000-home target Taken alone, major affordable development both completed and planned for Miles Platting and Newton Heath (1,289 homes), Cheetham (1,070 homes) and Ancoats and Beswick (806 homes) shows a healthy pipeline of projects in communities with high demand for affordable housing Substantial regeneration programmes will also further bolster the city’s housing investment outlook, with key schemes in Holt Town and Strangeways still to come online, while further significant housing investment is continuing at Victoria North and in our District Centres across In the last year, Manchester City Council reported record numbers of completions where 4,766 homes of all types and tenures were finished – contributing to the Housing Strategy target to build 36,000 homes up to 2032

Passengers travelling across Manchester's tram network were in for a surprise today (Friday 9 October) as 6,000 free books were given away on the city's trams by Read Manchester to mark World Mental Health which falls on Saturday.. The free book giveaway in partnership with Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) saw thousands of free reads placed on tram seats at the crack of dawn this morning - a book on every seat - and sent on their way from tram depots right across the tram network, ready to be picked up by passengers of all ages.. . The good read giveaway is part of Read Manchester's Take 10 to Read campaign which was first launched by Read Manchester in 2018 and is now promoted by the National Literacy Trust across the UK - and also this year worldwide through a world record attempt.. . The campaign highlights the wellbeing benefits of reading, and each year encourages people of all ages to spend 10 minutes reading on and around World Mental Health Day (10 October). to help improve their mental health.. . It complements wider work around the city by Read Manchester to encourage reading for enjoyment and help people discover the positive impact reading can have on learning, wellbeing and everyday life.. . This year's Take Ten to Read campaign, taking place during the National Year of Reading 2026, calls on people to explore their hobbies and interests through reading, with a simple message: whatever you're into, take 10 and read into it.. . Councillor Shazia Butt, Executive Member for Culture, Libraries and Leisure, Manchester City Council, said: . . "Good mental health is important for everyone whatever your age and escaping into the world of a book and reading - even just for ten minutes a day - is something that research shows can make a positive difference to how people feel.. . "Together with our partners at the National Literacy Trust we've been helping Mancunians and others find a love of books and reading for ten years now through Read Manchester, with over half a million books given away so far, and we hope passengers of all ages on the trams today enjoy our latest book giveaway and pick up a book and have a good read on us!". . A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

The opening marks Open Restaurant Group’s 9th restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Di At the heart of the restaurant will be a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, placing guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot; th From the grill, guests can expect the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallo t, alongside Turbot Steak, a bone-in cut finished with brown butter, green chilli and preserved lemon

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Red Light, Manchester’s award-winning LGBTQ+ cocktail bar, is making a surprise return to the city on Friday 9th October Reopening on Tariff Street in the heart of the Northern Quarter (next door to The Whisky Jar), the beloved venue reopens with a seductive new aesthetic, an expanded food and drink offering, and a revived music program Founded by Deana Ferguson, Red Light’s new home delivers the original concept fully realised: a refined yet welcoming sanctuary blending sleek booth seating, striking red lights, a bar, boutique club vibes, and an outdoor terrace open until 11 PM. The interior showcases the works The famous cocktail menu will return, featuring favourites like the Pink Picante, Pomme Verte – a popular twist on an appletini, Belfast Coffee, the famous spicy pickle martini Especiado and the Pornstar Chic, crafted with homemade passionfruit sorbet Red Light also introduces a brand-new savoury snack menu, including, Boquerones, Pickled Guindilla peppers, Gordal olives, Mini Croissant Butter Blondies from Pollen and homemade Salted Popcorn Ice Cream. To complement the elevated look and taste, Red Light has curated energetic, “Red Light has always been about bringing people together over exceptional drinks in an inviting, unpretentious environment. Our new location gives us the space to realise that vision fully, with the same soul and now a proper home for cocktails, food, and great music.”

candidates.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

candidates.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

candidates.evidence_text: Acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan is set to launch a new contemporary dining destination in Manchester this November Counter Manchester, the latest addition to the Open Restaurant Group portfolio and the first in Manchester city centre, promises to bring a ‘theatrical approach’ to dining. It follows the launch of Sheridan’s open-fire concept Arcadian in Didsbury last month The 60-cover restaurant will open in the Island Building on John Dalton Street. At its heart will be a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, placing guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors will feature four-metre elm trees, curved boot With Counter, the award-winning chef says he wants to challenge convention by exploring what British cooking can be, placing exceptional local produce at the heart of a menu shaped by flavours, ingredients and techniques from around the world The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot; th From the grill, guests can expect the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside Turbot Steak, a bone-in cut finished with brown butter, green chilli and preserved lemon

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan is set to launch a new contemporary dining destination in Manchester this November Counter Manchester, the latest addition to the Open Restaurant Group portfolio and the first in Manchester city centre, promises to bring a ‘theatrical approach’ to dining. It follows the launch of Sheridan’s open-fire concept Arcadian in Didsbury last month The 60-cover restaurant will open in the Island Building on John Dalton Street. At its heart will be a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, placing guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors will feature four-metre elm trees, curved boot With Counter, the award-winning chef says he wants to challenge convention by exploring what British cooking can be, placing exceptional local produce at the heart of a menu shaped by flavours, ingredients and techniques from around the world The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. candidates.evidence_text: Calling all craft lovers – one of Manchester’s best shopping and creative events is back next week with the return of the Great Northern Contemporary Craft Fair Taking place from Thursday 15 October to Sunday 18 October at the beautiful Victoria Baths, GNCCF brings more than 200 handpicked makers from across the UK to Manchester, with over 70 of the exhibitors appearing there for the first time Among this year’s newcomers are Welsh woodworker John Egan of Making Little, who transforms whole trees into beautifully crafted furniture and objects, and Northern Irish maker Caitlin Murphy, whose woven metal vessels blur the boundaries between textile and sculpture. Also look With prices ranging from affordable handmade gifts to collector-quality pieces, there’s something for every budget. And every exhibitor is selected by an independent panel of craft experts, so you can be sure to find quality pieces demonstrating originality and craftsmanship. Fro Alongside browsing and buying, visitors can enjoy an inspiring programme of talks, live demonstrations and hands-on workshops featuring exciting names from the worlds of craft, design and food. Highlights include free drop-in animation workshops using clay, food and other materia “GNCCF offers a connection you simply can’t get online or on the high street – the chance to meet the makers, hear the stories behind the work and invest in beautifully made pieces that will be cherished for years to come.”

But the images he returned with told a more complex story: shot in colour, they showed humanity and dignity alongside the hardship Sixty years later, photographer Simon Hill has retraced that journey. The conversation between their two bodies of work, now showing together at Jodrell Bank, builds a portrait of how much has changed since then and how much remains While Bulmer visited 16 locations across the North, Hill travelled to more than 50. From late 2024 to mid 2026 he crossed the historic seven counties from Newcastle to Liverpool, visiting former mining communities, coastal towns, city centres, remote landscapes, and the motorways In homage to Bulmer’s pioneering use of colour, much of Hill’s work was shot on Harman Phoenix 200, a contemporary colour film made in the North, and known for its unpredictable, textured qualities Bulmer’s North captured communities facing uncertain futures as the industries that defined them began to disappear. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. candidates.evidence_text: 43 years on from our only participation in the European Cup – a first-round defeat to Fenerbahce in 1968 – we qualified for the Champions League for the 2011/12 season. Now, as we approach our 150th game in this historic competition when we take on AEK Athens on Tuesday, we can say the Champions League has more than delivered on its guarantee of joy, heartbreak and everything in between. Having qualified for the continent’s hallmark cup competition in every season since Roberto Mancini led us there in 2011, we are currently on the longest ongoing run of appearances in the Champions League of any English side. The level of consistency required not to miss out in all that time speaks volumes to our domestic dominance particularly under Pep Guardiola but also with Mancini and Manuel Pellegrini. We have, after all, won the Premier League more than every other club combined since that 2011/12 season began. However, it’s not always been the same in Europe. With the finest of margins often deciding knockout ties between the most talented players on the planet, it felt for a long time as if City were destined never to lift the famous old trophy with the giant ear-shaped handles. That all changed in 2023, when Rodri curled home against Inter in Istanbul and Ederson produced a last-minute diving save to set the seal on a historic Treble. City had more than deserved it, having swept aside German champions Bayern Munich and defending winners Real Madrid in the previous rounds. But what you deserve isn’t always what you get in the Champions League. Bernardo Silva, who left City in the summer as our joint-most decorated player having been integral to all the successes under Guardiola, said this in his final interview with the club: “I think more of our teams could have done the same. “The final that we lost against Chelsea [2020/21] was a clear example. In my opinion, we were the best team in Europe that season and we played a really bad final. “The year that we lost to Real Madrid in the semi-final [2021/22], in the last minutes, I would say that we were the best team again in Europe that year for me. “The year that we lost to Madrid on penalties [2023/24], I also think that we were the best team that season in terms of quality of the game and in terms of the way that we performed. candidates.evidence_text: Football Manchester City FC Man City have tougher Champions League target after rule changes Manchester City should cruise through to a knockout place in the Champions League but a top-eight spot is difficult Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Simon Bajkowski Chief Man The Champions League is now into its third season since the first phase of the competition was ripped up and revamped. Rather than eight groups of four teams that all play six times, it is now a 36-team giant league table where everyone plays four opponents at home and a differen Two years is too small of a sample size for Enzo Maresca to know for certain exactly what Manchester City need to do to qualify, yet already some trends have emerged. And while the competition is commonly seen as having less jeopardy now, the race for a top-eight place means more A top-24 finish will guarantee City a place in the play-offs, and that bit should not be difficult to achieve. In the 2024/25 season there was only one team that accrued 11 points and did not qualify, while last season nine points was enough for Bodo/Glimt and Benfica to sneak in Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN! Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона! evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events Discover the Chamber Discover the Chamber Official Chamber Post FREE Courtyard Suite,, Broadhurst House Manchester, M1 6UE Tuesday 20 Oct 10am - 11:45am Book Now Discover Greater Manchester Chamber of Commerce Curious about how Chamber membership can support your business Join us for 'Discover the Chamber' , a first-of-its-kind event designed to introduce the wider business community to the Greater Manchester Chamber of Commerce and the opportunities available through our organisation and through membership Hosted at Chamber HQ, this informal and insightful session will provide an overview of the Chamber's history, purpose, impact, and future ambitions. You'll hear directly from our team and members about how businesses are making the most of their membership Whether you're considering joining, are new to the Chamber, or simply want to learn more about what we do, this event is an excellent opportunity to connect with our team, network with local businesses, and explore how membership can help your organisation thrive Who should attend? Business owners, leaders, entrepreneurs, and organisations from across Greater Manchester who want to expand their network, raise their profile, and access expert business support
